text.text: When something breaks, log it here, fix it, then write what happened without blame. Every postmortem ends in action items someone owns.
Incidents
Open any incident to find the full postmortem outline (timeline, impact, causes, fixes) ready to fill in.
Action items
Open actions
Incidents without a finished postmortem
Choosing a severity
Decide on the customer impact you can see right now, not on how the fix is going. Raise or lower it as you learn more, and say so in the incident channel.
SEV1: most customers cannot use the product, or data is at risk. Everyone who can help joins now.
SEV2: a core feature is broken for many customers, with no good workaround.
SEV3: a feature is degraded or broken for a few customers; a workaround exists.
SEV4: cosmetic or internal-only; fix in normal working hours.
When in doubt, start one level higher. Lowering a severity costs nothing; raising it late costs trust.

text.text: Who is the commander
The first on-call person to declare the incident, unless they ask to hand over. The commander coordinates and does not debug.
When to stop an incident
When the customer impact is gone and the cause is understood well enough to prevent a repeat tonight.
Thirty minutes every Thursday with the head of reliability and the action owners.
